lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: utility and fire-safety awareness

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic utility and fire-safety awareness task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: With an adult present for every step, the learner walks through their home locating three safety features one at a time: the main water shutoff valve, the electrical breaker or fuse box, and the nearest fire extinguisher or smoke detector.
safetyNotes: A trusted adult walks through the entire home with the learner and stays present for all three location checks; the learner is never in a utility area, near the breaker box, or near a fire extinguisher alone.
The learner points to and names each safety feature but does not touch, flip, test, or discharge the breaker switches, the water shutoff valve, or the fire extinguisher at any point.

If any of the three features is inaccessible, damaged, or unclear (for example, a locked utility closet or an unlabeled breaker panel), stop and use the simulation alternative instead of attempting to force access.

simulationAlternative.description: If any of the three safety features can't be located in the learner's home, use the floor-plan description on this task sheet instead: a single-story home with the water shutoff in a utility closet near the water heater, the breaker box on an interior garage wall, and a smoke detector in the hallway outside the bedrooms. Identify where each would typically be found in that layout and explain why its location makes sense.

materials: adult-or-local: access to the home's main water shutoff, breaker or fuse box, and a fire extinguisher or smoke detector, walked through together with a trusted adult

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l05-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l05-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l05-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l05-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Which of the three locations did you not know before this lesson, and how would you describe its location to someone else in your household who has also never been shown?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u02-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Feature location and non-operation compliance: Locates and correctly names all three features with the adult present the entire time, without touching, testing, or operating any of them. | Hazard reasoning: Explains a specific, accurate emergency situation and the consequence of not finding the feature quickly, for all three features. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner ask one other household member to walk them to the same three features from memory, without the learner leading, to check that the location knowledge has been shared beyond just the learner.

resources.title: utility and fire-safety awareness worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: With an adult present for every step, the learner walks through their home locating three safety features one at a time: the main water shutoff valve, the electrical breaker or fuse box, and the nearest fire extinguisher or smoke detector.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact utility and fire-safety awareness decision or action.
Model move 2: Before walking through the home, talk with your adult about why these three features exist and what each one is used for in an emergency.
Model move 3: With your adult present, walk to each of the three safety features one at a time.

Model check: Feature location and non-operation compliance: Locates and correctly names all three features with the adult present the entire time, without touching, testing, or operating any of them. | Hazard reasoning: Explains a specific, accurate emergency situation and the consequence of not finding the feature quickly, for all three features.

resources.title: utility and fire-safety awareness action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for utility and fire-safety awareness.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.

resources.title: utility and fire-safety awareness coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With an adult present for every step, the learner walks through their home locating three safety features one at a time: the main water shutoff valve, the electrical breaker or fuse box, and the nearest fire extinguisher or smoke detector.
Coach direction: Before walking through the home, talk with your adult about why these three features exist and what each one is used for in an emergency.
Learner prompt: Before you begin, guess in one sentence each: what do you think the water shutoff, the breaker box, and a fire extinguisher or smoke detector are each used for?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: utility and fire-safety awareness complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult present, walk to each of the three safety features one at a time. Stand next to it, name it out loud to your adult, and do not touch, flip, or test it.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My adult was present with me for all three location checks.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I located and named the main water shutoff without touching or turning it.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I located and named the breaker or fuse box without touching or flipping any switch.
Response 4 (t2-p4): I located and named the nearest fire extinguisher or smoke detector without touching, testing, or discharging it.

Equal-access rule: If any of the three safety features can't be located in the learner's home, use the floor-plan description on this task sheet instead: a single-story home with the water shutoff in a utility closet near the water heater, the breaker box on an interior garage wall, and a smoke detector in the hallway outside the bedrooms. Identify where each would typically be found in that layout and explain why its location makes sense.

resources.title: utility and fire-safety awareness minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Which of the three locations did you not know before this lesson, and how would you describe its location to someone else in your household who has also never been shown?

Success checks: Feature location and non-operation compliance: Locates and correctly names all three features with the adult present the entire time, without touching, testing, or operating any of them. | Hazard reasoning: Explains a specific, accurate emergency situation and the consequence of not finding the feature quickly, for all three features.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: utility and fire-safety awareness supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g8-u02-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional utility and fire-safety awareness condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Feature location and non-operation compliance: Locates and correctly names all three features with the adult present the entire time, without touching, testing, or operating any of them. | Hazard reasoning: Explains a specific, accurate emergency situation and the consequence of not finding the feature quickly, for all three features..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
